text: March, nineteen eighty-nine. Mark Kilroy, a twenty-one-year-old pre-med student from the University of Texas, crossed into Mah-tah-mor-ohs for spring break. Outside a bar, he vanished.
text0: March 1989. Mark Kilroy, a twenty-one-year-old pre-med student from the University of Texas, crossed into Matamoros for spring break. Outside a bar, he vanished.

text: His family searched. Authorities on both sides of the border searched. For weeks, nothing.
Then, on April first, a drug trafficker named Seh-rah-feen Er-nahn-dez drove straight through a police checkpoint. According to later accounts, he believed rituals had made him invisible.
text0: Then, on April 1st, a drug trafficker named Serafín Hernández drove straight through a police checkpoint. According to later accounts, he believed rituals had made him invisible.

text: Police followed him to a ranch outside the city: Rancho Santa Elena.
There they found a ritual cauldron… and fifteen bodies. One of them was Mark Kilroy.
Their leader was Adolfo de Heh-soos Kon-stahn-zo, El Pah-dree-no. He promised his followers that human sacrifice would protect them from bullets, and from the police.
text0: Their leader was Adolfo de Jesús Constanzo, El Padrino. He promised his followers that human sacrifice would protect them from bullets and from the police.

text: Weeks later, police cornered him in Mexico City. On May sixth, nineteen eighty-nine, he ordered one of his own followers to shoot him.
text0: Weeks later, police cornered him in Mexico City. On May 6th, 1989, he ordered one of his own followers to shoot him.

text: No trial. No answers. The cult that thought it was invisible was exposed by the one family that wouldn't stop looking. This is Plot Twist, with A. and R.
